request: Analyze GSE144133 for PMID 34252634 (Epigenetic rewiring of skeletal muscle enhancers after exercise training supports a role in whole-body function and human health.): how exercise affects gene expression as the paper intends.

final.assay: total RNA-seq (Ribo-Zero), human vastus lateralis biopsies (S2.4.p1)
final.subjects: 8 young sedentary Caucasian males, biopsy before and after 6 weeks of endurance training (S2.1.p1, S2.2.p1)
final.sample_inclusion: 16 biopsies; P6_2 and P8_2 excluded from DE for dermis contamination (S2.4.p1)
final.primary_estimand: within-participant change in skeletal muscle gene expression after 6 weeks endurance training (trained vs untrained), paired by participant
planned_contrasts: trained vs untrained, ~participant + training (S2.4.p1; S3.1.p2: 641 up, 176 down, FDR<0.1, of 13,108 detected genes)
final.normalization: kallisto v0.46 transcript quantification, summed to genes by sleuth (S2.4.p1)
final.paper_method: sleuth v0.30 likelihood ratio test ~participant vs ~participant + training; fold changes from Wald test (S2.4.p1)

paper_reconstruction.reasoning: Methods S2.4.p1 define the RNA-seq DE: kallisto + sleuth LRT comparing ~participant to ~participant + training, P6_2 and P8_2 excluded. Results S3.1.p2 report 641 up and 176 down at FDR < 0.1 with no fold-change cutoff. Methods mention 'Bonferroni corrected q-values' but results and Figure 1C state FDR < 0.1; recorded as a discrepancy and the FDR rule is used.

exclude_samples.GSM4281967: P8_2: excluded by the paper for high dermis-gene expression (S2.4.p1)

alignment.reasoning: Matrix columns (P1_1 ... P8_2) equal the title prefix before _R1_RNA; exact match on that derived key. Suffix _1/_2 agrees with the training column (Untrained/Trained) for every sample. Participant and training state come from the GEO characteristics.

matrix.matrix_type: linear normalized abundance (sleuth-normalized gene-level kallisto estimates, scaled reads per base)
matrix.reasoning: GEO: 'csv file with estimated abundances' from kallisto 0.46 summed to genes by sleuth 0.30; semicolon-delimited, 12,900 Ensembl genes (paper: 13,108 detected), already filtered. Profile: 1.3% integer values; median-of-ratios size factors across the 16 samples are 0.93-1.17, i.e. already normalized; within the 8 pre samples the variance/mean ratio is 0.21 (mean 0.5-1), 0.32 (1-2), 0.52 (2-5), 0.88 (5-10): sub-Poisson, impossible for read counts, so the values are scaled abundances, not counts. Column sums up to 1.65e6 on a gene subset rule out TPM. Sleuth itself models log(x+0.5) of these normalized values, so a log-scale linear model is the matching route.

candidates.reason_rejected: sub-Poisson variance at low means and size factors ~1 show the values are normalized/scaled, not read counts; a first attempt with this reading (moved to _previous/) gave 15 DEGs with baseMean ~1-5 for well-expressed muscle genes, consistent with the count scale being wrong
column sums exceed 1e6 on a filtered gene subset

design.reasoning: Paper estimand: trained vs untrained within participant (S2.4.p1 ~participant + training). Interventional pre/post design; no control group, so the effect is a within-subject pre-post change. Single male sex; no sex split.

final.method: limma (moderated t, empirical Bayes) on log2(x+0.5) sleuth-normalized abundances

paper_route.reason: sleuth needs per-sample kallisto abundance.h5 with bootstraps, which are not deposited; only the gene-level normalized abundance table is available

deviations: limma moderated t on log2(x+0.5) replaces the sleuth LRT on log(x+0.5) with bootstrap-informed technical variance; same model terms (~participant + training) and same pseudocount

method.reasoning: sleuth fits a linear model on log(x+0.5) of normalized abundances with shrunken variance; limma on log2(x+0.5) with participant blocking is the closest available executor. DESeq2 rejected because the values are not counts.

final.deviation_note: paper FDR < 0.1 applied to limma BH-adjusted p; audit at workflow default padj < 0.05

threshold.reasoning: S3.1.p2 and Figure 1C: FDR < 0.1, no fold-change cutoff.
